tool.name: Local API / Edge Service Interface
tool.purpose: Define the local-first service surface that lets hardware be operated, inspected, configured, updated, and diagnosed without depending on cloud infrastructure.
scope: Local dashboard and maintenance app interface
Safe command routing for robots, chargers, machines, cameras, printers, and instruments
Versioned API contracts, schemas, receipts, and health endpoints

projects.role: Foundation study bundle for electronics, SiC MOSFETs, and embedded Linux.
projects.use_when: A future board or Linux device needs a clean service model before hardware/software split is frozen.
projects.how: Use embedded Linux concepts to design a minimal local service: /health, /version, /logs, /config, /diagnostics. Treat this as a lab standard before implementing on real boards.
projects.production_part: Embedded Linux boards, lab fixtures, power-board diagnostics.

projects.role: Offline cartridge architecture, manifest, local-first storage, and integrity.
projects.use_when: The cartridge reader must expose status, verify/commit actions, and error receipts to the host without cloud dependency.
projects.how: Expose a serial/USB local protocol for cartridge_inserted, manifest_verified, commit_started, commit_done, rollback, and fault states. Provide JSON receipts for every read/write/verify cycle.
projects.production_part: Cartridge reader service, host validator, local maintenance UI.

projects.role: First EVT/CAD implementation of the 8MB module.
projects.use_when: The prototype needs a PC test utility or browser-facing local service for bench validation.
projects.how: Map firmware serial commands to a small local API and generate validation receipts: flash_id, read_verify, write_verify, power_loss_recovery.
projects.production_part: PCBA test service, fixture app, cartridge service bridge.

projects.use_when: The flight controller needs safe local diagnostics before any tethered or powered motor test.
projects.how: Expose read-only health endpoints first: imu_state, barometer_state, flash_log_state, arming_state, battery_state. Keep motor/arming commands behind a physical-safe gate.
projects.production_part: Ground test dashboard, tether-test service, blackbox log extractor.

projects.role: Open-source quadruped robot research and productization study.
projects.use_when: The robot needs local operation, gait state visibility, calibration, and service diagnostics.
projects.how: Bridge ROS2 topics/services into a local dashboard with strict command permissions: observe, calibrate, enable torque, safe pose, walk mode, emergency stop.
projects.production_part: ROS2 service UI, field maintenance interface, education dashboard.

projects.role: Agriculture automation, CNC-style gantry, electronics, firmware, web app, and tool ecosystem.
projects.use_when: A farm-side system must keep working with poor internet or no cloud access.
projects.how: Provide local queue, axis status, tool status, water state, job receipt, manual jog, stop command, and offline sync boundary.
projects.production_part: Local farm controller, maintenance app, toolhead service interface.

projects.role: Open-source lab microscope and precision positioning platform.
projects.use_when: The microscope must expose capture, focus, illumination, stage movement, and calibration locally.
projects.how: Use local HTTP/API commands for image capture, focus sweep, stage move, illumination level, objective profile, and calibration receipt export.
projects.production_part: Microscope local server, calibration dashboard, lab evidence API.

projects.role: Open satellite ground-station stack: antenna, SDR, Linux station, observation workflow.
projects.use_when: The station must be monitored locally for RF chain, observations, scheduler, disk, network, and rotator state.
projects.how: Expose local status page and API for sdr_detected, antenna_profile, observation_active, last_pass, decode_status, storage_free, and fault history.
projects.production_part: Ground-station dashboard, RF commissioning service, observation receipt generator.

projects.role: High-performance open-source 3D printer engineering and kit/productization study.
projects.use_when: A printer kit needs local control, status, and calibration without depending on remote services.
projects.how: Treat Moonraker/Klipper-like local API surfaces as the pattern: printer_state, heaters, bed_mesh, print_job, emergency_stop, config snapshot, first-print receipt.
projects.production_part: Printer local UI, commissioning dashboard, service workflow.

projects.use_when: The charger needs local status, diagnostics, and integration while never allowing unsafe remote enablement.
projects.how: Use a strict safety hierarchy: local API may request charging settings, but the safety controller owns diode/GFCI/ground/stuck relay/temp fault decisions. Expose RAPI/MQTT/HTTP read-only status first.
projects.production_part: EVSE local dashboard, commissioning probe, charge log service.

projects.use_when: A vision product needs video, events, model thresholds, and privacy state without cloud dependency.
projects.how: Expose RTSP/HTTP/snapshot/event endpoints plus privacy controls, local-only mode indicator, camera health, model version, and storage retention settings.
projects.production_part: Camera appliance UI, local AI event bridge, privacy evidence API.

projects.project: BeagleV-Fire / Milk-V Duo RISC-V edge bundle
projects.role: RISC-V edge computing, FPGA, AIoT, embedded Linux, deterministic IO.
projects.use_when: An edge board becomes a gateway, accelerator, or deterministic IO node.
projects.how: Create a board agent with /health, /temperature, /gpio, /camera, /fpga, /benchmark, /update_status, and signed local evidence receipts.
projects.production_part: Edge service daemon, local web UI, factory validation endpoint.

projects.role: Plastic recycling and small manufacturing machine ecosystem.
projects.use_when: A machine control box needs local recipes, cycle state, heater/motor telemetry, and guarded commands.
projects.how: Expose recipe view, temperature status, cycle counters, fault history, guard state, maintenance timers, and receipt export. Gate start/reverse/heater commands behind physical interlocks.
projects.production_part: Machine HMI, workshop dashboard, process-run logger.

projects.project: NASA JPL Rover / OpenAMRobot research bundle
projects.role: Rover mechanics plus modern AMR/ROS2 robot stack.
projects.use_when: A mobile robot needs local operation, diagnostics, route/docking state, and safe command control.
projects.how: Bridge ROS2/Nav2/micro-ROS into a local UI with health topics, pose/map state, wheel/encoder diagnostics, E-stop state, docking result, and commissioning receipts.
projects.production_part: AMR local operator dashboard, docking validation app, field service tool.

stages: Record which repo/firmware/API docs define the service. Pin commit/release and license.
Classify every operation as observe, configure, calibrate, actuate, update, or emergency.
Decide which commands are read-only, physically gated, software-gated, or prohibited.
Choose serial, USB, HTTP, WebSocket, MQTT, BLE, ROS2 bridge, or local Unix socket.
Define request/response JSON, error codes, version, timestamps, and device identity.
Build local UI pages for health, state, logs, settings, calibration, and receipts.
Store command result, safety state, operator action, firmware version, and pass/fail evidence.
Run fixture tests through the same API used by field service and generate a signed receipt.
Use the service to diagnose without opening the product unless a hardware fault is proven.
checklist: Identity
Device exposes product_id, hardware_rev, firmware_rev, serial_number, api_version.
Health
Device exposes power, thermal, storage, network, sensor, actuator, and fault state.
Safety gate
All dangerous commands require local preconditions and cannot bypass hardware interlocks.
Read-only first
Initial bring-up API is read-only until basic electrical and mechanical safety is validated.
Offline-first
All core operation and diagnostics work with no internet connection.
Error vocabulary
Every failure has a stable code, human message, recovery instruction, and severity.
Command audit
Every configuration, calibration, update, and actuation request generates a receipt.
Rate limits
Commands cannot be spammed fast enough to destabilize motors, heaters, flash, relays, or UI.
Timeouts
Every API call has a deterministic timeout and fallback state.
Versioning
API changes are explicit and backward compatibility is tracked.
Update boundary
Firmware/config updates require hash verification and rollback path.
Privacy
Camera/log/network APIs disclose what data is captured, stored, and exported.
Local credentials
Admin commands require local authentication or physical-presence confirmation.
Factory mode
Factory/test commands are disabled or locked out in normal user mode.
pass_gates: The device can be identified locally without cloud access.
The operator can see health, state, fault, and version locally.
Dangerous commands are impossible unless physical and software gates are satisfied.
Every command returns a structured response with status, code, message, and timestamp.
Power cycle does not erase fault history needed for diagnosis.
A factory test receipt can be generated from a clean device using only local tools.
Network loss does not leave motors/heaters/relays/charging in an unsafe state.
A failed firmware/config update rolls back or enters a clearly visible recovery state.
risks: Default to read-only; require physical enable; enforce command allowlist.
Dashboard E-stop treated as real safety stop
Label software stop clearly; require hardware E-stop for robots/machines/EVSE.
All diagnostics and receipts must run offline on LAN/USB/serial.
Require local credentials, pairing, physical button, or signed service token.
Version drift between UI and firmware
Expose api_version and compatible_min/max in every response.
Classify logs; provide export redaction and retention controls.
MQTT/WebSocket floods MCU or ROS graph
Rate-limit, queue, backpressure, and command timeout.
Factory debug mode leaks into production
Factory mode flag, build-time lock, physical jumper, audit event.
Hash inputs, include firmware/source versions, use monotonic sequence, optional signature.
Dual image/dual manifest, hash check, rollback, visible recovery UI.
endpoints: Read product identity, serial, hardware revision, firmware revision, API version.
Read current operating mode and state-machine node.
Read active and historical fault codes.
Request software stop; not a substitute for hardware E-stop.
Start a calibration routine when safety preconditions are true.
Read latest validation or command receipt.
Write configuration only after schema validation and compatibility check.
Stage signed firmware/config update; do not activate until verified.
